description.summary: compositor-managed dock visibility and reserved area

protocol.description:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.
This protocol hands the overall show/hide behaviour of a dock to the compositor. The dock surface stays an ordinary wlr-layer-shell surface and keeps drawing its own content; what moves into the compositor is the decision whether the dock is shown, the animation that carries it in and out, and the area it reserves on the output.
The compositor owns these decisions because it is the only party that can coordinate them with everything else it animates: toplevel maximize and unmaximize, fullscreen exit, the multitask overview, output reconfiguration, and its own window layout. A client that animates the dock itself races all of that, and a client that unmaps the dock pays a re-map and repaint cost on every reveal.
What the client reports is what the compositor cannot observe: the user's visibility mode, temporary interaction holds (an open menu or popup, an icon drag), forced visibility for conditions the compositor cannot detect (the launcher), and which outputs arm the edge wake-up strip. Everything else - pointer position, overlap of toplevels with the dock strip, the fullscreen state of the active toplevel, the multitask overview - is observed by the compositor directly.
The client keeps owning the output the dock lives on: it is the client that decides to move the dock when the user touches another output's edge, and the compositor only reports which output was touched. This is why the output policy exists: the compositor must know on which outputs to arm the wake-up strip, because the client cannot create one of its own.
For a managed dock the compositor keeps the surface mapped at all times and hides it by moving it out of the output instead of unmapping it, so a reveal never waits for a new buffer. The client must not animate the dock's own size, position, or visibility: no resizing the surface toward the edge, no hiding the window, and no overlay strip of its own for edge wake-up detection. The client's own content animation inside the dock is unaffected.
A managed dock must already have the wlr-layer-shell role, and must be anchored to exactly one edge along its thickness axis: top or bottom for a horizontal dock, left or right for a vertical one. The two ends along the dock's length axis are not constrained: a full-width horizontal dock anchored to the bottom edge is anchored to bottom, left and right, and is a valid managed dock. Neither the thickness nor the length is part of this protocol: both are read from the layer surface state.
The compositor must reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

interface.name: treeland_dock_manager_v1

description.summary: factory for managed docks

interface.description:
A global that creates treeland_dock_v1 objects for privileged DDE clients implementing a dock. The compositor must reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.
At most one dock may be managed per output, and a dock need not exist on every output. A client with a single dock that moves between outputs keeps one treeland_dock_v1 object for its whole lifetime: the object follows the surface, and moving the surface to another output does not require a new object.
A dock moves itself between outputs, so the compositor cannot detect a conflicting dock at get_dock time. A managed dock whose surface moves to an output that already has a managed dock is a client error, and the compositor posts output_conflict on the dock that moved there. That error is a protocol error like any other: it terminates the client connection, it is not recoverable for the dock alone, so a client must never let two managed docks meet on one output.

description.summary: factory errors

entry.name: already_dock_surface
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a treeland_dock_v1 object

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the wl_surface is invalid or does not have the layer-shell role

entry.name: invalid_mode
entry.summary: the initial visibility mode is not a known visibility_mode value

entry.name: invalid_output_policy
entry.summary: the initial output policy is not a known output_policy value

request.name: get_dock

description.summary: start managing a layer-shell surface as a dock

request.description:
Start managing the given layer surface as a dock, with the given user visibility mode and output policy as the initial values. Passing them here rather than defaulting avoids reserving space and arming strips for a dock whose settings are about to change.
The surface must already have the wlr-layer-shell role; otherwise the compositor posts invalid_surface. Only one treeland_dock_v1 object may be associated with a given wl_surface; a second attempt is a protocol error already_dock_surface. An unknown mode or policy value is a protocol error invalid_mode or invalid_output_policy, since there is no previous value to keep.
Immediately after this request the compositor sends the current target visibility with the visibility event.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: the layer-shell surface to manage as a dock

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the manager

request.description: Destroy the treeland_dock_manager_v1 object. Managed docks created through this manager are not affected.

interface.name: treeland_dock_v1

description.summary: compositor-managed dock

interface.description:
The dock object hands the dock's overall visibility and reserved area to the compositor.
The compositor derives the target visibility as follows.
1. Baseline from the mode: always_visible is shown; smart_hide is shown; always_hidden is hidden. 2. Hide triggers: in always_visible the dock is hidden while the compositor's active toplevel is fullscreen, on any output; in smart_hide the dock is hidden while an xdg-shell toplevel overlaps the strip along the dock's edge. 3. Holds cancel the hide triggers of step 2 only. If a step 2 trigger was the only reason the dock was hidden, cancelling it reveals the dock, reported with reason interaction. A hold never reveals a dock hidden by its mode in step 1: creating a hold while the mode is always_hidden leaves the dock hidden. When the last hold is destroyed the compositor re-evaluates from step 1 with the same delays and the same priority as any other trigger: it does not hide immediately and it does not skip a wait the ordinary rules would apply. 4. Pointer contact with the wake-up strip reveals the dock in every mode, including smart_hide while a toplevel overlaps the strip, and produces an edge_wake event naming the output whose edge was touched. When the touched output is not the one the dock is on, the reveal waits for the client's move; see the cross-output rule below. Once the pointer leaves the dock and the strip, steps 1 to 3 decide again, after the ordinary delay. 5. The multitask overview overrides the result to shown. On exit the compositor removes the override and re-evaluates from step 1; it does not restore whatever was shown before the overview opened, and it never changes the reported mode. 6. Forced visibility set with set_forced_visibility overrides the result to shown, including over a fullscreen hide trigger. Each reason is cleared independently, and clearing the last one re-evaluates from step 1 with the ordinary delays.
Steps 1 to 3 are the only steps that hide: nothing else hides a dock they leave shown. Steps 5 and 6 override the result to shown and therefore also apply to a dock that steps 1 to 3 leave hidden; apart from those overrides, only step 4 and the step 3 case reveal a dock that steps 1 to 3 leave hidden.
The compositor keeps the surface mapped and performs the reveal and hide animation itself, including interrupting an animation in flight in the opposite direction. Durations, easing, and the delays between a trigger and the animation are compositor policy and are not part of this protocol.
Reserved area: for a managed dock the compositor owns the space reserved on the output and derives it from the visibility mode alone, not from the current visibility: space is reserved in always_visible and not otherwise, even while the dock is hidden by a fullscreen toplevel. A fullscreen toplevel occupies the whole output regardless of the dock. The reserved strip spans the entire edge of the output and is as thick as the dock; the dock's own length does not narrow it, so a shorter, centered dock reserves the same strip as a full-width one. The client should leave the layer-surface exclusive zone at 0; the compositor must ignore a managed dock's layer-surface exclusive zone and reserve the strip itself, exactly once.
The strip that is watched for overlap in smart_hide and for edge wake-up in every mode is the same one: the entire edge of the output, as thick as the dock. A managed dock does not need treeland_region_watch_v1, and the client must not create its own wake-up surface.
Wake-up strips are armed on every output the output policy allows and are not armed on any other output: with primary_only the strip is armed only on the compositor's primary output, with any_output on every output. Contact with an armed strip produces an edge_wake event and reveals the dock, subject to the cross-output rule below; the client decides from that event whether to move the dock to the reported output.
Edge wake-up across outputs: when the touched strip is on an output other than the dock's own, the compositor must not begin the reveal before the client moves the dock. It reveals the dock once the surface is on the touched output, or after a compositor-chosen timeout if the client never moves it. A reveal or hide animation already in flight follows the surface to its new output and must not leave a frame of the dock on the old one.
Changing the anchored edge: the client may change the edge its surface is anchored to at any time, for example when the user picks another dock position. The compositor re-derives the geometry from the new layer surface state and may run a transition that hides the dock along the old edge and reveals it along the new one; the exact transition is compositor policy and it does not by itself change the target visibility or produce a visibility event. The client must not add an animation of its own on top of it.
Unknown values passed to set_visibility_mode, set_output_policy, or set_forced_visibility are ignored: the previous value stays in effect and no error is raised, so that a newer client can talk to an older compositor. The initial values passed to get_dock are not covered by this rule and are rejected as protocol errors.
Lifecycle: the client must destroy its hold objects before destroying the dock object, and must destroy both before destroying the wl_surface they belong to. Destroying the dock object destroys the holds created from it, so a client that destroys the dock first must not send destroy on any of its holds afterwards. If the wl_surface is destroyed first, the compositor destroys the dock and all of its holds as a fallback for crashed or misbehaving clients, and the client must not send any further request on those objects afterwards.

description.summary: dock errors

entry.name: output_conflict
entry.summary: the surface moved to an output that already has a managed dock; reported as a protocol error that terminates the client connection

enum.name: visibility_mode

description.summary: user setting for when the dock is shown

enum.description: The user's dock visibility preference. The mode is the user's setting and is distinct from the current visibility reported by the visibility event.

entry.name: always_visible
entry.summary: the dock is shown and reserves space; it is hidden only while the active toplevel is fullscreen

entry.name: smart_hide
entry.summary: the dock is hidden while a toplevel overlaps the dock strip, and reserves no space

entry.name: always_hidden
entry.summary: the dock is hidden and reserves no space; it is revealed when the pointer touches its edge

enum.name: output_policy

description.summary: where the edge wake-up strip is armed

enum.description: The client's policy for which outputs arm the edge wake-up strip, and therefore for the outputs the dock may be shown on. It only selects the outputs whose edge wake-up strip is armed; the compositor never moves the dock itself and the client still owns the output the dock lives on. The policy says nothing about where the dock may be right now: a dock that is temporarily on another output keeps working and keeps its reserved area, it simply cannot be woken from that output.

entry.name: primary_only
entry.summary: the edge wake-up strip is armed only on the compositor's primary output

entry.name: any_output
entry.summary: the edge wake-up strip is armed on every output

enum.name: forced_visibility_reason

description.summary: reason why the client forces the dock visible

enum.description: Reasons accepted by set_forced_visibility. Different reasons are independent: each one is set and cleared on its own, and the dock stays visible while at least one of them is set.

entry.name: launcher
entry.summary: the application launcher is shown; the compositor cannot observe it

enum.name: visibility_reason

description.summary: why the compositor settled on this visibility

enum.description: Why the compositor's target visibility is what the visibility event reports. The reason describes the decision at the moment the target changed; it is not kept up to date afterwards - a hold being created or released for a dock that stays shown does not produce a new event. It is informational and must not be used by the client to decide visibility or to run a competing animation.

entry.name: mode
entry.summary: the reported visibility mode alone decides it

entry.name: edge_wake
entry.summary: the pointer touched the dock edge and revealed the dock

entry.name: window_overlap
entry.summary: smart_hide: a toplevel overlaps the dock strip

entry.name: fullscreen
entry.summary: always_visible: the active toplevel is fullscreen

entry.name: interaction
entry.summary: a hold cancelled the hide trigger that was hiding the dock

entry.name: multitask_view
entry.summary: the multitask overview is forcing the dock visible

entry.name: other
entry.summary: another compositor reason not covered by this enum

request.name: destroy

description.summary: stop managing the surface as a dock

request.description:
Stop managing the surface as a dock. The compositor stops deciding its visibility, animation, and reserved area, releases the reserved strip, stops arming wake-up strips for it, and restores the surface to the position and size derived from the layer-shell state alone, placed as visible. Holds created from this object are destroyed with it.
The client regains control over the dock's presentation from that point on, including its layer-surface exclusive zone: the compositor no longer reserves anything for this surface, so a client that wants reserved space again must set an exclusive zone itself.

request.name: set_visibility_mode

description.summary: report the user's visibility preference

request.description:
Report the user's current dock visibility preference. The initial value comes from get_dock.
The compositor re-evaluates the dock's visibility when the mode changes and applies the same delays and the same animation it applies to any other trigger.

request.name: set_output_policy

description.summary: report which outputs arm the edge wake-up strip

request.description:
Report the client's output policy. The initial value comes from get_dock.
The compositor arms the edge wake-up strip on every output the policy allows and removes it from the others; it does not move the dock itself. When the policy becomes primary_only, moving the dock back to the primary output is the client's job.

arg.name: policy
arg.summary: which outputs arm the edge wake-up strip

request.name: get_hold

description.summary: block automatic hiding for one interaction

request.description:
Create a hold: one object per interaction that must keep the dock from hiding, for example an open menu, an open popup, or an icon drag in progress.
A hold cancels the hide triggers and nothing else; it never overrides the mode. The full rule is step 3 of the interface description: a hold cancelling the only reason the dock was hidden reveals it, while a hold created while the mode is always_hidden does not, and the last hold being released triggers a re-evaluation with the ordinary delays instead of an immediate hide.
Holds are counted by object lifetime, so several interactions can overlap without any counter bookkeeping in the client: each hold is released by destroying it.

request.name: set_forced_visibility

description.summary: report a condition that must show the dock

request.description:
Set or clear a reason that forces the dock visible regardless of the visibility mode, of the hide triggers, and of holds. This is not a hold: a hold prevents hiding, forced visibility requires showing, and only the client can report the conditions that need it - the compositor cannot observe the launcher.
Each reason is set and cleared independently: sending visible is 1 sets the reason, sending visible is 0 clears it. Sending the value that already applies is allowed and has no further effect. While a reason is set the dock is shown even in always_hidden mode. The reserved area does not change because of a forcing reason; it follows the mode, as described in the interface description.

arg.name: reason
arg.summary: the condition being set or cleared

arg.name: visible
arg.summary: 1 to set the reason, 0 to clear it

event.name: visibility

description.summary: the target visibility changed

event.description:
Sent once when the dock object is created, to report the initial target visibility, and afterwards whenever that target changes.
visible is the target the compositor is driving the dock toward; it is not a report that an animation finished, and there is no event for the end of an animation. The reason argument is informational; see visibility_reason.
The event reports the result of the compositor's decision and never asks the client to show or hide anything: the client keeps the surface mapped and must not react by animating, resizing, or hiding it.

arg.name: visible
arg.summary: the target visibility, 1 for shown and 0 for hidden

arg.name: reason
arg.summary: why the compositor settled on this visibility

event.name: edge_wake

description.summary: the pointer touched the dock edge on an output

event.description:
Sent every time the pointer touches the wake-up strip on an output where the strip is armed, whether or not the dock's target visibility changes and whether or not the dock is already on that output.
The event reports which output the user touched; moving the dock there is the client's decision, taken according to its own policy. The client may ignore an edge_wake whose output is the output the dock is already on. The compositor sends nothing further on this object because of that move: if the dock is revealed by the contact, the accompanying change of target visibility arrives as a separate visibility event with reason edge_wake.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output whose edge the pointer touched

interface.name: treeland_dock_hold_v1

description.summary: a temporary block on automatic hiding

interface.description: One hold object per interaction that must keep the dock from hiding. The hold is released by destroying it, and is destroyed by the compositor if the dock object or its wl_surface is destroyed first.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: release this hold

request.description: Release this hold. Releasing the last hold makes the compositor re-evaluate the dock's visibility with the same delays and priority as any other trigger; it does not hide the dock immediately.
